title: Nucleic Acid Extraction Using the MagMAX™ CORE Kit on a Magnetic Particle Processor
author: Nathaniel Higdon
materials: MagMAX™ CORE Nucleic Acid Purification Kit

Aliquot the appropriate volumes of working stock solutions of Wash Solution 1 (500 µL per sample), Wash Solution 2 (500 µL per sample), and Elution Buffer (90 µL per sample) into separate sterile containers. Adding an additional 10-15% volume of each reagent is advised to cover losses from pipetting errors Using low bind pipettes can aid in the prevention of reagent loss and further reduce losses form pipetting It is advised to use foil seals or have some type of container to prevent light from reaching reagents. Wash 1 solution is light sensitive.
Proceed at once to the magnetic particle processor.

steps.title: Prepare Instrument Software
steps.instruction: Ensure the appropriate program (e.g., KingFisher Flex heated script: MagMAXCORE_Flex.bdz) is downloaded and uploaded to the magnetic particle processor.

steps.title: Prepare Samples
steps.instruction: Remove samples from freezer or refrigerator and thaw on ice or a cold block inside a Biological Safety Cabinet (BSC).

substeps.instruction: Ensure all caps/lids are secured.
Clean dirty outer surfaces with bleach, bleach wipes, ethanol, or appropriate disinfectant.
Dry containers after cleaning.

steps.title: Initialize Instrument
steps.instruction: Turn on the machine, locate and select the desired program name on the display screen, and push start.

steps.title: Prepare Reagent Plates
steps.instruction: In the clean room, prepare reagent plates according to the specified volumes and arrangement.

substeps.instruction: Plate 2: Add 500 µL Wash 1 per well.
Plate 3: Add 500 µL Wash 2 per well.
Plate 4: Add 90 µL Elution Buffer per well.
Plate 5: Prepare Tip Comb.
Loosely cover plates with a seal to prevent cross-contamination during transport.

steps.title: Prepare Proteinase K/Bead Mix
steps.instruction: Prepare the PK/Beads mix in a sterile container and aliquot into Plate 1.

substeps.instruction: Add 20 µL of MagMax™ CORE Magnetic Beads to 10 µL of MagMax™ CORE Proteinase K Solution per sample.
Gently vortex the mix.
Add 30 µL of the mix to each appropriate well in a deep well 96-well plate (Plate 1).

steps.title: Prepare Lysis/Binding Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare the Lysis/Binding solution in a light-protected sterile container (e.g., wrapped in a glove).

substeps.instruction: Mix 350 µL of MagMax™ CORE Lysis Solution and 350 µL of MagMax™ CORE Binding Solution per reaction.
Add 2 µL of Xeno™ RNA Internal Control per total number of reactions and vortex.
Note: This solution is stable for 24 hours and should be prepared last to minimize sample time in buffer and light exposure.

steps.title: Transport Reagents
steps.instruction: Place all prepared reagent plates into a transport container and move them to the extraction/sample room.

steps.title: Add Samples to Plate 1
steps.instruction: Vortex each sample briefly at high speed (considering sample fragility) and add to the deep well plate containing 30 µL PK/Beads.

substeps.instruction: For whole blood: add 100 µL of sample per well.
For all other sample types and controls: add 200 µL of sample per well (100 µL is acceptable if original volume is insufficient).
Return remaining samples/controls to ice.

steps.title: Mix Samples
steps.instruction: Seal the plate with aluminum foil (or equivalent) and mix the samples.

substeps.instruction: Decontaminate the plate and remove from the BSC.
Shake on an orbital shaker at moderate speed for 2 minutes (alternatively, mix by pipetting up and down).
Wait a few seconds or centrifuge at low speed if aerosols/droplets are present on the seal.

steps.title: Add Lysis/Binding/Xeno Solution
steps.instruction: Immediately after vortexing the Lysis/Binding/Xeno™ solution, pipette 700 µL into each sample/control well in Plate 1 and seal the plate.

substeps.instruction: Perform an additional shake to ensure full mixing.
Perform a rapid centrifuge to ensure no sample is on the seal.

steps.title: Load Instrument
steps.instruction: Load the plates into the processor as prompted by the display screen.

substeps.instruction: Open the sliding door.
Insert the requested plate (X) into the presented slot and click start.
Repeat until all plates are loaded.

steps.title: Run Program and Collect Elution
steps.instruction: Close the sliding door and press start to initiate the program (approx. 25-30 minutes).

substeps.instruction: At the end of the program, remove the Elution plate (Plate 4) from the front of the sliding door and seal it immediately.
Press start repeatedly to move the turntable and remove all remaining plates.
Press Stop and power down the machine.

steps.title: Post-Extraction Storage and Cleanup
steps.instruction: Store the extracted DNA/RNA or use immediately.

substeps.instruction: Store at -60°C or less if not used immediately.
Aliquoting into other plates or individual tubes is optional.
Disinfect all exposed surfaces of the machine and record run data/sample information.

description: Notes: With the exception of the addition of the Xeno ™ Internal Control all reagent preparation should be, and is highly recommended, to be performed in the clean room. It is highly recommended that prior to beginning the extraction procedure that the laboratorian annotate all the pertinent information in the extraction worksheet (Nucleic Acid Extraction using the MagMAX™ CORE Nucleic Acid Purification Kit on a Magnetic Particle Processor Worksheet) including but not limited to lot numbers, reagent kit numbers, expiration dates, etc., and sample positions on the 96-well plate.
